Lecture 6 Randomized Algorithms Spring 2015 Quicksort Divide and conquer algorithm but work mostly in the divide step rather than combine. Sorts “in place” like insertion sort and unlike mergesort (which requires O(n) auxiliary space). Diﬀerent variants: • Basic: good in average case • Median-based pivoting: uses median ﬁnding • Random: good for all inputs in expectation (Las Vegas algorithm) Steps of quicksort: • Divide: pick a pivot element x in A, partition the array into sub-arrays L, consisting of all elements <x , G consisting of all elements >x and E consisting of all elements = x. • Conquer: recursively sort subarrays L and G • Combine: trivial Basic Quicksort Pivot around x = A[1] or A[n] (ﬁrst or last element) • Remove, in turn, each element y from A • Insert y into L, E or G depending on the comparison with pivot x • Each insertion and removal takes O(1) time • Partition step takes O(n) time • To do this in place: see CLRS p. 171 3 6.046J

Lecture 6 Randomized Algorithms Spring 2015 Basic Quicksort Analysis If input is sorted or reverse sorted, we are partitioning around the min or max element each time. This means one of L or G has n −1 elements, and the other 0.
